business_problem: Notion's legacy event-logging architecture could not scale with rapid user growth, online indexing, AI features, and multi-destination integrations without driving up tooling costs and distracting a lean engineering team with infrastructure work.
solution_summary: Notion moved to a fully managed event-driven architecture on Confluent Cloud to make product events available in real time for analytics, integrations, and Notion AI. The platform replaces a brittle pattern of third-party tools and custom connectors with one managed Kafka backbone that scales clusters up and down, expands retention on demand, and streams changes directly into destinations such as Amazon S3, Snowflake, and PostgreSQL. Schema Registry and stream processing help the team enrich and govern events, while the AWS-native deployment fits cleanly into Notion's existing infrastructure. The most important use case is AI: as users update pages and workspace content, Confluent immediately synchronizes those changes into Notion's vector database so RAG search and content-generation workflows always use current context. By offloading Kafka operations, the engineering team can focus fully on new product features instead of running infrastructure.

solution_components.name: Confluent Cloud
solution_components.role: Acts as Notion's managed event backbone for analytics, integrations, and AI synchronization.

solution_components.name: Amazon S3
solution_components.role: Receives real-time event streams for storage and analytics use cases.

solution_components.name: Snowflake
solution_components.role: Stores and analyzes streamed event data for downstream decision-making and product workflows.

solution_components.name: Schema Registry
solution_components.role: Supports real-time capture, enrichment, and governance of user events.

data_flow: Workspace and application events stream through Confluent Cloud, flow into destinations like Amazon S3 and Snowflake, and are synchronized into Notion's vector database so RAG search, content generation, and connected-app integrations use current workspace context.
business_outcome: Notion gained a scalable real-time AI backbone, tripled productivity, lowered operations cost, and freed the data platform team to spend all of its time on new features rather than Kafka operations.
architecture_clues: Notion keeps its Kafka backbone on AWS and uses fully managed connectors to move data into storage and application systems.
The streaming platform keeps a vector database synchronized in real time for RAG search and generation.
The engineering team is evaluating additional Confluent features such as managed Flink and autoscaling on top of the current event-driven design.
